beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps dense image detail in a carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process repeatedly updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method separates dense image state from the compact recurrent thought that updates it. The encoder first turns the low-resolution image into features. The features are partitioned into windows before the thought process reads them. The DQ-CTM step repeats across ticks while sharing parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense carrier back into a super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier through shared thought ticks
params.note: The loop belongs to the thought stage, not the whole flow.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines both the dense feature field and the token-preserving window partition that feeds the thought process.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as a dense field, so spatial information is present before recurrent thinking begins. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into that dense feature field. The window operator partitions the field while keeping every token available to the process.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before it is windowed

terms.label: encoder maps the low-resolution image to features

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five listed methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read directly, because compact thought does not make this model the cheapest entry. CATANet is the smallest listed method. RFDN is only slightly larger than CATANet. IMDN remains below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger still at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model listed
params.note: Smallest first; values are parameter counts in millions.
